source.title: Interpretability analysis on a pathology foundation model reveals biologically relevant embeddings across modalities
source.citation: Nhat Dinh Minh Le et al., 2024
source.authors: Nhat Dinh Minh Le; Ci-Yue Shen; Neel Patel; Chintan Shah; Darpan Sanghavi; B. Martin; Alfred Eng; Daniel Shenker; Harshith Padigela; Raymond Biju; S. A. Javed; Jennifer A. Hipp; J. Abel; Harsha Pokkalla; S. Grullon; D. Juyal

page_placements.theme: Interpretable sparse dictionary features across model domains

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether selected SAE features behave like semantically selective and reproducible units in a pathology vision model, using correlation, entropy, and cross-training comparisons. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the superposition hypothesis and discusses polysemanticity, but does not test sparse feature overlap, a sparsity-dependent transition, or capacity competition. Rows capture its results directly relevant to whether SAE features are selective and reproducible; cited results and other analyses are not included.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on a pathology ViT (PLUTO) and compares features from SAEs trained on different datasets. This bears on V5's stability claim in a new setting, a vision foundation model. It runs no toy-model or capacity experiments. Its neuron-versus-SAE monosemanticity results concern a vision model, not an LLM, so they do not bear on V4 as worded.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that PLUTO embedding dimensions are polysemantic and SAEs yield relatively monosemantic, interpretable biological features. These features emerge in later layers, are robust to scanner and stain, and generalize to an out-of-domain dataset. They also call SAE features universal across separately trained SAEs, based on example feature pairs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAEs on pathology vision-model embeddings and evaluates interpretability, cell-count correlations, and feature reproducibility. It does not use the original toy-model setup or test superposition geometry or a sparsity-dependent transition.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported feature representations vary across PLUTO layers: earlier layers correlate more with color features, while later layers show stronger cell-feature associations. The study also compares SAE training datasets and evaluation domains.

fits_no_version.finding: In a pathology ViT, individual embedding dimensions are polysemantic. SAE features are more selective: SAE-1736 correlates ρ=0.7 with plasma cells and ρ<0.1 with other cell types, entropy 0.42, versus 0.65 for neuron 148 (max 0.70).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: V4 extended to vision models: real vision transformers contain sparse features that an SAE recovers more monosemantically than neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: The plasma-cell SAE feature's correlation pattern holds on the out-of-domain CPTAC dataset. Monosemantic cell-type SAE features appear only in later layers (plasma cells from layer 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-recovered features in vision models generalize across data domains and emerge with depth.

record.problems: The semantic analysis includes manual inspection, and the reported reproducibility examples are selected features rather than a comprehensive assessment of all SAE dimensions. Numerical uncertainty estimates are not stated. The paper notes that it uses a vanilla SAE and leaves other pathology foundation models and latent-space interventions for future work.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, geometry or phase transition.
No test of capacity competition or of importance-dependent dedicated dimensions.
No alternative causes of polysemanticity are examined.
No LLMs studied; the SAE recovery of sparse features is in a vision transformer only.
Completeness of the dictionary is untested. Systematic cross-seed or cross-size feature matching is absent. Whether features are canonical (e.g., splitting across expansion factors) is not examined.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Fractions of dead, ultra-low-density and common features across SAE training datasets and expansion factors 1/8/16/32, showing dictionary composition depends on training data and size.
Fractions of stain-specific vs cross-stain SAE dimensions (8.0% both, 12.2% H&E-only, 47.2% IHC-only).

record.verdict_notes: The only results bearing on V5 are illustrative cross-SAE feature pairs. There is no systematic matching statistic, so support is narrow. The reader's limits_scope label on r1/r2 was misapplied: those rows show selectivity, which is not a V5 claim, and an untested part (completeness) should not be labelled limits_scope. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature sparsity sweep, overlap geometry, or transition is tested.
The study does not test whether limited capacity causes features to compete, or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
It does not investigate alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or test whether polysemanticity alone indicates superposition.
The models are pathology vision models, not LLMs; the study does not test feature distribution across LLM neurons.
Tests selected features' semantic selectivity and reproducibility, but not completeness of the SAE dictionary or whether SAE features are uniquely canonical units of the model.
The study does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: PLUTO
rows.operation_detail: Measured the correlation of the SAE dimension with the five cell-count features.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation with plasma cell counts
rows.note: The paper reports this as the highest correlation for plasma cells and says SAE-1736 has minimal correlation (ρ < 0.1) with other cell types; this supports selectivity for the tested cell-count concepts, not completeness of the dictionary.
rows.check: This is the selectivity (monosemanticity) of the best plasma-cell SAE feature, a selection value (the maximum correlation among 3072 dimensions). V5 concerns completeness, stability and canonicity, not selectivity. The neurons-polysemantic / SAE-monosemantic contrast is a vision analogue of V4, but V4 names LLMs. Moved to fits_no_version.

source_check.locator_found: §2.2; §3.3–3.4: maximum plasma-cell correlation and identification of SAE-1736.
source_check.problem: The value is a selected maximum across SAE dimensions, not an estimate of typical feature selectivity.

rows.subject: PLUTO
rows.operation_detail: Compared entropy of the five-cell-type correlation distribution for an SAE feature and an embedding dimension.
rows.measure: Entropy of the absolute-correlation distribution over five cell types
rows.baseline: PLUTO dimension 148: S = 0.65; maximum possible entropy Smax = 0.70
rows.note: Lower entropy indicates greater selectivity for the measured cell types; it does not establish a complete or canonical feature basis.
rows.check: This entropy comparison of SAE-1736 (S=0.42) against PLUTO dim 148 (S=0.65) measures monosemanticity versus neurons in a vision model. It is not V5's stability or canonicity, and V4 is restricted to LLMs. Both dimensions are hand-picked maxima. Moved to fits_no_version.

source_check.locator_found: §3.4: absolute-correlation distribution over five cell types and entropy comparison.

rows.subject: PLUTO
rows.operation_detail: Compared corresponding SAE feature activations from two SAEs trained on different datasets.
rows.measure: Correlation between the two SAE activations
rows.note: The paper reports both dimensions as representing plasma-cell abundance.
rows.check: This is a single illustrative feature pair chosen by the authors, not a systematic match rate across all dimensions. The value is correct (ρ=0.96).

source_check.locator_found: §5.3: SAE-1736 from the 1M-trained SAE and SAE-2541 from the TCGA-trained SAE, ρ = 0.96.

rows.subject: PLUTO
rows.operation_detail: Compared corresponding SAE feature activations from two SAEs trained on different datasets.
rows.measure: Correlation between the two SAE activations
rows.note: The paper reports both dimensions as representing abundance of anthracotic macrophages.
rows.check: Same as r3: one illustrative pair (ρ=0.91). There is no population-level reproducibility statistic.

rows.subject: PLUTO
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated cell-feature correlations for SAE dimensions on an out-of-domain dataset.

conditions.value: CPTAC; cutaneous melanoma and head and neck cancer

rows.measure: Robustness of cellular-feature correlations and plasma-cell representation across domains
rows.value: The text states that the results were confirmed on CPTAC and that the plasma-cell representation was robust across domains; numerical values are not stated in the text.
rows.note: The text gives an explicit qualitative conclusion; the plotted values are not reported numerically.
rows.check: This applies the same SAE to an out-of-domain evaluation set. It shows the feature-to-concept correlation generalizes, not that independently trained dictionaries converge. No numbers are given in the text (Figure 6 only).

relationships.condition: Selected plasma-cell and anthracotic-macrophage features, SAEs trained on 1M vs TCGA data, PLUTO layer 12
relationships.reason: Matching features from separately trained SAEs correlate highly (ρ=0.96, 0.91; r3, r4), but only for hand-picked examples.
relationships.display_finding: Matching features from separately trained SAEs correlated at ρ=0.96 and 0.91, though only hand-picked examples were checked.

source_check.condition: Selected plasma-cell and anthracotic-macrophage features, SAEs trained on 1M vs TCGA data, PLUTO layer 12
source_check.reason: r3 and r4 establish recurrence of these two selected features, with activation correlations of 0.96 and 0.91. Support is confined to these examples; completeness and full-dictionary canonicity remain untested.

relationships.condition: Dictionary composition across SAE training data and expansion factor (Table S1, text-based)
relationships.reason: Based on Table S1 text, not rows. Ultra-low-density features are 88.2% (TCGA SAE) vs 20% (1M SAE), and 0.3% to 53% across expansion factors 1 to 32. The dictionary's makeup depends on training choices.
relationships.display_finding: Ultra-low-density features made up 88.2% of the TCGA SAE versus 20% of the 1M SAE, and ranged from 0.3% to 53% across expansion factors 1 to 32.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Dictionary composition across SAE training data and expansion factor (Table S1, text-based)
source_check.reason: Table S1 confirms the stated ultra-low-density fractions, but measures activation-frequency categories rather than feature identity, completeness or canonical decomposition. Changing these fractions across datasets or dictionary widths does not establish failure of V5; no corresponding feature-stability comparison is reported for this condition group.
